deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics and no derivations. It is a continuous page of an administrative memorandum (Gutachten) addressed to the 'Hohes Curatorium' of the University of Göttingen, then in the Kingdom of Hannover. It responds to General J. J. Baeyer's proposal, made around 1861-62, for a Central European arc measurement ('Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung'). The argument across the surrounding pages runs as follows.

(1) Previous page: the electric telegraph is a new instrument ideally suited to determining longitude differences. The writers therefore ask for two things: a telegraph line connecting the Göttingen observatory to the Göttingen telegraph station, and the purchase of a registering apparatus (chronograph). This is Hansen's improved design, built by the instrument maker Ausfeld in Gotha for 200 Thaler.

(2) This page: with these, the longitude differences between Göttingen and all other observatories linked to telegraph stations could be determined with previously unattainable accuracy. A second, portable registering apparatus, movable between telegraph stations, would later allow equally accurate longitude differences for a system of points distributed over the whole country.

(3) The value of such a country-wide system of astronomical longitude determinations would depend especially on combining it with corresponding systems of latitude differences and gravity differences. The gravity differences would be obtained by comparative pendulum measurements, as set out in the enclosure ('Anlage').

(4) This should be recommended for attention as the project proceeds. The results obtained could surpass, in a significant way, the achievements of similar undertakings in the East and West (presumably the Russian-Scandinavian and Anglo-French arc measurements), as General Baeyer hopes.

(5) A later insertion in a lighter hand at the foot of the page adds a caveat. For acquiring the necessary apparatus (the pendulum instruments) one should wait for a favourable opportunity, and the writers therefore refrain from going into it further at present.

(6) The next page continues: Hannover would cooperate if the Central European states united. A purely Hannoverian execution would have independent value, but not enough to pursue without other countries joining.

Scientifically, the substance is the geodetic programme of combining astro-geodetic longitude, latitude and gravity (pendulum) data to study the figure of the Earth. The 'Anlage' referred to is presumably the more technical enclosure. Nothing on this page needs reconstruction in formulas.

results.what: Proposal to determine longitude differences between observatories by electric telegraph with a chronograph (registering apparatus), and to extend this to a country-wide network with a portable chronograph
results.usually_credited_to: US Coast Survey (Walker, Bond, Bache, 1840s-50s); in Europe adopted in the 1850s-60s; organized internationally by Baeyer's Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung (1862)

results.what: Recommendation to combine longitude, latitude and gravity (relative pendulum) measurements for studying the figure of the Earth
results.modern_name: Combined astro-geodetic and gravimetric determination of the geoid / Earth figure (arc measurement programme)
results.usually_credited_to: Baeyer (1861 memorandum 'Über die Größe und Figur der Erde'); the gravimetric idea goes back to Clairaut, Stokes (1849) and others

deep.surprise_reason: This is an administrative recommendation, probably a jointly authored Göttingen faculty Gutachten responding to Baeyer's Gradmessung proposal. It requests a telegraph line and a chronograph and recommends combining longitude, latitude and pendulum gravity measurements. All of this was standard geodetic practice and the content of Baeyer's own programme. There is no mathematics. Riemann's involvement in such a Göttingen report is a minor biographical detail and not a scientific discovery.
transcription_corrections: 'für ein System im ganzen Lande vortheilhafter[?] Punkte' should most likely read 'vertheilter Punkte' (points distributed over the whole country). This fits the handwriting and the sense.
'wie General Baeyer die Stellung ausspricht[?]' should likely read 'wie General Baeyer die Hoffnung ausspricht'.

The struck-through interlinear words '[-und Schwere-]' sit above 'Wichtigkeit und Bedeutung' and were deleted. The inserted gravity point is instead made in the main text ('Schwereunterschiede ... Pendelmessungen').
On the next page, 'in bedeutender Weise übertragen würden' is probably 'übertroffen würden' (surpassed), which fits the sentence begun on this page.

The two faint lines at the bottom are a later insertion in a lighter hand: 'Doch dürfte für die Beschaffung der dazu nöthigen Apparate eine günstige Gelegenheit abzuwarten sein und wir enthalten uns daher hierauf gegenwärtig näher einzugehen.' The transcription has this correctly; it is an addition, not part of the original running text.
